lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 50, which lets a search word starting with an exclamation mark hide names.
It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
After Ctrl+F you type a query, such as report, then draft with an exclamation mark.
lines.say: After control F you type a query, such as report, then draft with an exclamation mark.

lines.caption: The query is folded to lower case and split into words; the exclamation mark is kept.
Each plain word must be in the name, and each exclamation word must not be.
The list, the tree and the subfolder search all use that one check, so they agree.
You wanted only the names without a dash, which used to take Select by Pattern and Invert Selection.
The prefix is an exclamation mark, not a dash, so a search for a dash still finds dashes.
Each word of the query is one condition.
Normalizing and splitting the query leave the exclamation mark and the backslash alone.
The one matching function inverts the test for exclamation words; a lone one, or one after a backslash, is plain text.
Every view already called that function, so none of them changed.
Here is what each query lists in a folder of five sample files.
A dash finds the two dashed names, and an excluded dash finds the other three.
Report, excluding draft, finds only report dot t x t.
lines.say: Report, excluding draft, finds only report dot T X T.

lines.caption: A backslash before the mark, or the mark alone, searches for the mark as text.
The whole change is a few lines in that one matching function.
To undo it, revert this PR; nothing is saved anywhere.
The PR changes one source file and adds its test, this page and its narration.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was built on the existing matching function, the search test from issue 21, and issue 22's spec.
It builds cleanly, and the rule alone gave the expected result for all six queries.
Under Xvfb, a dash still finds the dashed names, and an excluded dash finds the other three.
lines.say: Under X V F B, a dash still finds the dashed names, and an excluded dash finds the other three.

lines.caption: Report excluding draft finds one file, and the escaped and lone marks find bang name.
All four sandbox tests passed, and an auditor agent found all six screenshots right.
The icon view can't be checked: Thunar switches to the details view during any search.
Each search is checked by copying its results into a folder; CI repeats it and posts its own screenshots.
A fresh review agent found no high or medium bugs, and four low ones.
An icon view test was added, then dropped, because the audit showed the details view instead.
The rest are kept: full-width marks also exclude, and a backslash only escapes plain words.
CI's own review is in the code review comment on the PR.
After the merge, try it in your own folders, and run the split view crash check.
Part 3. Nothing depends on issue 22, so only your own check remains.
Try an excluded dash in a real folder, then run the split view check.
In short: put an exclamation mark before a word to hide the names that contain it.
